sections.title: Quick guide
sections.text: Quick guide Pseudo-nitzschia  is a genus of marine diatoms. Some species can produce domoic acid, a neurotoxin that can travel through marine food webs. The presence of the genus alone does not mean a harmful bloom is occurring.

sections.title: Identification and life cycle
sections.text: Identification and life cycle These microscopic photosynthetic diatoms have silica cell walls. They reproduce by cell division and can undergo sexual reproduction. Reproductive phases, from the July Field Note.

sections.title: Harmful algal blooms and the 2015 event
sections.text: Harmful algal blooms and the 2015 event Some species, including  P. australis  and  P. multiseries , can produce domoic acid. Bloom risk depends on species, abundance, environmental conditions and toxin production. 2015 harmful algal bloom and fisheries effects.

sections.title: Domoic acid in food webs
sections.text: Domoic acid in food webs Domoic acid can move from diatoms into shellfish and small fish, then to seabirds and marine mammals. Exposure may cause neurological problems. It is heat-stable and is associated with amnesic shellfish poisoning in humans. Neurotoxicity illustration from the Field Note.
